deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is ch. 4 (end) and the start of ch. 5 of Euler's 'Tractatus de numerorum doctrina' (E792, c. 1750). Here phi(n) denotes the number of k with 1<=k<=n and gcd(k,n)=1. The previous page derived phi(M p^n) = p^(n-1)(p-1) phi(M) for a prime p not dividing M, and from it the product formula phi(prod p^lambda) = prod p^(lambda-1)(p-1).

§133 (multiplicativity). If gcd(M,N)=1, phi(M)=m and phi(N)=n, then phi(MN)=mn. On the page this is a direct corollary of the product formula in §132: the prime-power factorizations of M and N are disjoint. A direct argument is sketched in §§137-139.

§134 (Euclid's theorem). Suppose p were the largest prime. Put M = 2·3·5·7···p. Then M would share a factor with every number greater than 1. But gcd(M, M±1)=1 (implicit step, mine: any common divisor divides 1). So M+1 (or M-1 when M>2) is greater than 1 yet shares no prime with M. That contradicts the assumption.

§135. More strongly, by §132 the number of integers below M that are coprime to M is phi(M) = prod_{q<=p}(q-1) = 1·2·4·6···(p-1). This grows as more primes are multiplied in, so besides M-1 there are many other units.

§136. Each of these m = phi(M) numbers in [1,M] coprime to M is a prime greater than p or a product of primes greater than p. (The number 1 is tacitly included; it is neither.) This gives many witnesses to primes beyond p.

§137 (periodicity). gcd(k,M) depends only on k mod M. So each block [jM+1,(j+1)M] contains exactly m units mod M. Hence #{k<=NM : gcd(k,M)=1} = Nm for every N.

§138. Symmetrically, [1,MN] contains Mn numbers coprime to N and Nm numbers coprime to M. A number is coprime to MN iff it is coprime to both M and N.

§139. The earlier result is restated: if gcd(M,N)=1, the count of units in [1,MN] is mn, and these lie in both the sets of size Mn and Nm. No independent derivation of mn from the two counts is given here. That would need the CRT, which is listed in the footnote.

Footnote (Euler's marginal notes, a list of gcd lemmas):
- (i) Heading: gcd and its computation.
- (ii) If gcd(A,B)=1, there is a multiple xA with xA ≡ C (mod B). This is solvability of a linear congruence, the key to the CRT.
- (iii) If gcd(A,B)=1, then gcd(A^i,B^j)=1.
- (iv) If gcd(A,B)=gcd(A,C)=1, then gcd(A,BC)=1.
- (v) If prime p | AB, then p|A or p|B (Euclid's lemma).
- (vi) If gcd(A,B)=1, there exist m,n with mA-nB=1, or equal to any given number (Bézout).
- (vii) If phi=gcd(A,B), then gcd(A/phi, B/phi)=1.
- (viii) If a ≡ r (mod b), then na ≡ nr (mod nb).
- (ix) If a = mb + r, then common divisors of (a,b) and of (b,r) coincide.
- (x) If gcd(a,b)=1 and a>b: a=mb+p with p<b, b=np+q with q<p, and so on until remainder 1 (Euclidean algorithm).

§140 (ch. 5). Definition of residue: if a = mb + r with 0<=r<b, then r is the residue of a on division by b.
errors: §136: the list 'primes or composites of primes >p' tacitly includes 1, which is neither; a trivial omission.
§134: 'M ad M-1 ... certe sit primus' needs M-1>1 (fails if p=2, M=2), but the alternative M+1 covers this; the step gcd(M,M±1)=1 is left implicit.

§§138-139 do not by themselves prove phi(MN)=mn; they restate §133 (which rests on §132's product formula). The combinatorial derivation from the counts Mn and Nm would require the CRT, which Euler lists only as a marginal note. This is a gap in presentation, not an error in the result.

phi(primorial p#) = prod_{q<=p}(q-1); units mod p# are 1 or products of primes >p
results.modern_name: totient of primorial / reduced residue system mod p#

results.modern_name: periodicity of gcd(k,M) in k mod M

deep.surprise_reason: The Tractatus (published 1849) is a well-known source for Euler's totient and its multiplicativity, and the remaining material is classical elementary number theory.

checkable.asserts: phi of primorial equals product of (q-1) (§135)
M+1 need not be prime but its prime factors exceed p (§134/136)

checkable.sympy: all(min(factorint(k)) > 7 for k in range(2, 211) if gcd(k, 210) == 1)
checkable.asserts: units mod 2·3·5·7 greater than 1 have only prime factors >7 (§136)

checkable.sympy: sum(1 for k in range(1, 5*30+1) if gcd(k, 30) == 1) == 5*totient(30)
checkable.asserts: count of units mod M up to NM is N·phi(M) (§137)

checkable.sympy: sum(1 for k in range(1, 12*35+1) if gcd(k, 12) == 1 and gcd(k, 35) == 1) == totient(12)*totient(35)
checkable.asserts: coprime to MN iff coprime to both; count mn (§§138-139)
Bézout coefficients exist for coprime A,B (footnote)
na mod nb = n·(a mod b) (footnote)

transcription_corrections: Transcription matches the image closely; the 'sunt' in §138 has a stray printing mark (asterisk-like dot) which is not part of the text.
In the footnote, 'Si A et B sint numeri primi' should be read as 'primi inter se' (coprime), as the context requires.
